successors.name: Kingdom of Hadramawt
successors.text: the Wadi Bayhan core, Cliopatria's last Qataban shape (183); Cliopatria gives all of it to Hadhramaut in 184

successors.name: Himyarite Kingdom
successors.text: the Himyarite share of the divided kingdom: the page gives no boundary, so this repeats the Qataban shape of 183 and must be shared with Hadhramaut by the renderer's ordering

ledger.x: c. 625 BCE: Qataban stands as a centralised kingdom at Timnaʿ. 'Qatabān had developed into a centralised state centred around Timnaʿ by the late 7th or early 6th century BCE'; 'In the late 7th century BCE, Qatabān and the nearby kingdom of Ḥaḍramawt were initially allies of the king' Karib'il Watar. -625 is a reading…
Late 5th century BCE: Qataban free of Saba.
After 420: Qataban reaches the Bab al-Mandab.
183: the kingdom of Qataban ends, its territory divided by Hadramawt and Himyar.

wars.name: Sabaean destruction of Awsan
wars.outcome: Karib'il Watar of Saba destroyed Awsan in the late 7th century BCE; 'Saba, after defeating Awsan, divided the territory between two of its other allies at the time', Qataban and Hadhramaut.

wars.name: Karib'il Watar's war with Qataban
wars.outcome: Qataban, first an ally of Karib'il Watar, fell out with Saba (hostilities later broke out with the king Yadʿʾab, page paraphrase) and in the 6th century 'had come under the control of Sabaʾ'.

wars.name: Qatabanian coalition against the Sabaeans
wars.outcome: The page gives no outcome: 'At one point in the 1st century BCE, Qatabān formed a coalition with Ḥaḍramawt, Radman, Maḏay, and the' Arab nomads against the Sabaeans.

wars.name: Aelius Gallus's expedition to Arabia
wars.outcome: The Romans 'attempted to conquer Saba around 26/25 BCE' and gave up the siege of Marib because of 'heat exhaustion'; no border moved.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any Qatabanian frontier; the Wadi Bayhan core is approximate and the south-western reach to the Bab al-Mandab (-350..-111) and the Sayhad desert frontier are softer still.
